title: Understanding the Problem
text: The problem involves comparing two linear regression models: one using the original design matrix X and the other using the mean-centered design matrix X̃. Both models aim to minimize the sum of squared errors.

title: Mean-Centering Effect
text: Mean-centering the design matrix affects the intercept term but not the slope coefficients. This is because mean-centering shifts the data but does not change the relationships between variables.

title: Intercept Term
text: When the data is mean-centered, the intercept term in the regression model becomes zero. This is because the mean of each predictor variable is subtracted from the data, aligning the data around the origin.

title: Slope Coefficients
text: The slope coefficients (β) in the original model and (γ) in the mean-centered model are the same. This is because mean-centering does not affect the relationships between the variables, only the intercept.

title: Conclusion
text: Based on the properties of mean-centering, are the slope coefficients β and γ the same?
